findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "delete_strategy" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Permanently delete a strategy by its ID. Use this only when the user explicitly asks to delete a strategy. Always confirm the strategy name and ID before deleting." → after: "Archive a stopped strategy that has no open positions. Strategies are never hard-deleted: this hides the strategy from the default lists and keeps the strategy and its backtests, and it can be restored with POST /strategies/{id}/unarchive. Use this only when the user explicitly asks to delete or rem"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.

findings.title: Tool removed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "update_strategy_status" is no longer advertised. Removal can precede a shadowing replacement from another server.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "evaluate_strategy" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Evaluate a strategy against current live market data to check if entry or exit signals are active — read-only signal check, does NOT place any orders. Returns the current asset price and any order intents the signals would produce. Use this when the user asks whether a strategy should be entering or" → after: "Evaluate a strategy against current live market data to check if entry or exit signals are active. It places no orders and opens no positions, but each call records the evaluation: it updates the strategy's last_evaluated_at and evaluation_count and adds an agent_evaluations audit row. Returns the c"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_strategies" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "List the strategy definitions saved HERE, in this service -- drafts and backtested strategies authored through chat. This store never knows deployment state: for what the user is actually running (live or paper deployments, balances, PnL), use list_platform_strategies instead. Returns id, name, asse" → after: "List the caller's saved strategies, including drafts, backtested strategies and server-managed paper strategies. Returns id, name, asset and status. Use paper execution status for current run state and balances. list_platform_strategies covers separate platform deployments."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
